summary: Kent County, DE, CCC-erected tower west of Viola (1935), raised to 113 ft by 1937 and removed 2004-2006; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: First designed as a 100-foot tower; total height 123 ft to the top of the hurricane deck rail (113 ft to the cabin floor)
facts.status_note: Removed between 2004 and 2006; the statewide account gives 2002 to 2006 for all five Delaware towers; no description of the site today

events.note: Erected by Civilian Conservation Corps men under Emergency Conservation Work funds, on a one-acre site about 1.5 miles west of Viola
Placed in service in the fall of 1935
State FY 1937 report says the 13.5-foot section was inserted and the cabin replaced during the summer of 1936; the FY 1936 report describes the same work as still planned
Association dates the added section that raised the cabin floor to 113 feet to 1937
Sliding aluminum-frame windows with blur glass installed
Removed between 2004 and 2006 per the register and the association; exact year not given

corrections.why: 36.6 m is 120 ft. The register gives a total height of 123 ft (37.5 m), and the 1936 state report gives 123 ft to the top of the hurricane deck rail (113 ft to the cabin floor).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 123 ft total. The 1936 state report gives 113 ft to the cabin floor and 123 ft to the top of the hurricane deck rail. The association gives 113 ft after 1937. Recorded as 123 ft (37.5 m) total, with the 113-foot cabin-floor figure in design.

The FY 1936 state report describes the added section as planned. The FY 1937 state report says it was inserted in the summer of 1936. The association dates the 113-foot height to 1937. The events list carries both: the state's 1936 account and the association's 1937 date.
The register and the association give 2004 to 2006 for this tower. The Delaware overview gives 2002 to 2006 for all five state towers. The tower-specific span is recorded.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 36.6 m is 120 ft and is corrected to 123 ft (37.5 m). Build, registration and removal are well sourced. The site today is not described by any source read, so no access level or visit details are recorded. No staffing or fire records were found for this tower, so none are recorded. The Kemnow page carries a January 2004 photo credit (Gary Weber) with no image URL, so no photo record was added. The brief's note that the two Delaware towers share a register number does not match the pages: the NHLR number is US 53 and the FFLOS number is US 74, so no conflict is recorded. The state's own FY 1937 report dates the insertion to summer 1936; the story gives that account next to the association's 1937 date.
